t_9c0f6540 (RCA, cluster-fuxiaogao-gkedemos-gitops-pilot-20260918-14123-97b2c62a) — done. Complete result:

## Root cause

`checkout` is stuck at 3/4 because the **namespace ResourceQuota `payments-quota` rejects every new pod at admission** — not an image, crash or scheduling problem. Revision 2 raised the container memory request from `64Mi` to `256Mi`, and 4 replicas × `256Mi` (+ `pricer` 2 × `64Mi`) = `1152Mi` against a hard cap of `832Mi`.

Proof — `deployment/checkout` condition `ReplicaFailure`, `2026-09-18T18:29:21Z`:

`pods "checkout-8448b6988-jg768" is forbidden: exceeded quota: payments-quota, requested: requests.memory=256Mi, used: requests.memory=832Mi, limited: requests.memory=832Mi`

## Evidence

- `resourcequota/payments-quota` (`uid ebc637ff-0184-4546-abdd-b46f32372011`): `spec.hard.requests.memory: 832Mi`, `status.used: 704Mi`. Owner `platform-team`, ticket `CAP-418`.
- New RS `checkout-8448b6988` — desired `4`, current `2`. Old RS `checkout-595f7f4d8c` (rev 1) still holds `1` pod. `status`: `readyReplicas: 3`, `unavailableReplicas: 2`.
- Revision diff (rev 1 → rev 2): `requests.memory` `64Mi` → `256Mi`; image `hashicorp/http-echo:1.0` → `1.0.0`. The image is healthy — `Successfully pulled image "hashicorp/http-echo:1.0.0" in 474ms`, both new pods `Running 1/1`, `0` restarts.
- The bump is unjustified by demand: `kubectl top pods` shows every checkout pod at `1Mi` actual memory.
- No `LimitRange`, no HPA, no PDB in `payments`. Node has `6170284Ki` allocatable — ample; this is a quota wall, not capacity.

## Proposed patch (GitOps)

In `tasks/b-0011` (branch `run/gitops-pilot-20260918-141238/b-0011`), `Deployment payments/checkout`, revert the request:

```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 64Mi   # was 256Mi
```

That lands at `4 × 64Mi + 128Mi = 384Mi` of `832Mi`, leaving surge headroom. Do **not** raise `payments-quota` instead: it is `platform-team`-owned under `CAP-418`, and covering 4 × `256Mi` plus `maxSurge: 25%` would need `≥1408Mi` — a 69% quota increase for a workload using `1Mi`.

## Transient action

None. Argo CD sync of the corrected manifest creates a new ReplicaSet and the rollout completes on its own; the failing RS backs off but is superseded. No manual delete or restart required.

## Operational note

My preflight failed check `4`: the pinned kubeconfig is correct for this cluster, but `KUBECONFIG` is **not exported** in this profile's environment (no `.env` at the profile home), so a bare `kubectl` resolves to `gke_fuxiaogao-gkedemos_us-central1_platform-agent-host`. Every command above was explicitly pinned with `--kubeconfig`, confirmed as context `gke_fuxiaogao-gkedemos_us-central1-a_gitops-pilot-20260918-141238`. Worth re-pinning the profile.

**Worth remembering:** in `payments`, `payments-quota` caps `requests.memory` at `832Mi` and is `platform-team`-owned under `CAP-418` — raising a per-pod memory request there is a breaking change unless the replica-count × request product is checked against that cap first.

## Grounding

Cluster [gitops-pilot-20260918-141238](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/clusters/details/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-20260918-141238?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) (`us-central1-a`, project `fuxiaogao-gkedemos`), namespace `payments`, [deployment checkout](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/deployment/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-20260918-141238/payments/checkout/overview?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) `uid b850ca62-2731-4fdc-a51a-e710e56dfbb9`, `generation 2`. Argo CD app `b-0011`: `Synced` / `Progressing`.

Commands (all `--kubeconfig`-pinned, read-only), run `2026-09-18T18:31Z`–`18:36Z`: `get deploy checkout -o yaml`, `get rs -o wide`, `get pods -o wide`, `get resourcequota -o yaml`, `get limitrange`, `get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp`, `top pods`, `get hpa,pdb`, `get nodes`, `-n argocd get applications`. Failure events observed `18:29:21Z`–`18:29:29Z` (latest combined event `18:29:29Z`).

Git manifests could not be read — `git clone` is refused outside a leased GitOps workspace and `github.com` egress times out from this agent; the revision-1 spec was recovered from the live ReplicaSet `checkout-595f7f4d8c` instead.

## Sources

- `mcp__developer_knowledge__answer_query` — maxSurge/ResourceQuota interaction during rolling updates; cites `docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/planning-scalability` and `docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/best-practices-for-running-cost-effective-kubernetes-applications-on-gke`.
- Live cluster state via read-only `kubectl` (above).

t_67ff293b (GitOps remediation, platform) — done. Complete result:

The fix is proposed and awaiting a human merge — [PR #1](https://github.com/gke-agentic/kage-eval-20260918-claude-1/pull/1). `checkout` is still `3/4` Ready; nothing recovers until that PR merges.

## What's wrong

`payments/checkout` sits at `3` of `4` replicas. The new ReplicaSet `checkout-8448b6988` cannot create its last pods — the Deployment carries `ReplicaFailure/FailedCreate` and `Progressing=False (ProgressDeadlineExceeded)`.

## Why

- **Quota rejection at admission, not a workload fault** — this morning's revision raised `resources.requests.memory` on container `web` from `64Mi` to `256Mi`. At `replicas: 4` that is `1024Mi`, plus `pricer` at `128Mi` = `1152Mi`, against ResourceQuota `payments-quota` `hard requests.memory=832Mi` (used `704Mi`). The API server refuses: `pods "checkout-8448b6988-jg768" is forbidden: exceeded quota: payments-quota, requested: requests.memory=256Mi`. The image pulls fine and every running pod is healthy.
- **Argo CD is Synced but Degraded** — Application `b-0011` is at revision `ab52216` of `run/gitops-pilot-20260918-141238/b-0011`, i.e. faithfully applying the broken desired state. `selfHeal: true` and `prune: true` are on.
- **No safe interim action exists, and none was taken** — a manual `kubectl rollout undo` or in-place resource edit would be reverted by Argo CD's self-heal within a minute, and direct cluster mutation is outside my mandate. Merging the PR is the fastest path to recovery.

## What to do

- **Merge [PR #1](https://github.com/gke-agentic/kage-eval-20260918-claude-1/pull/1)** — one line in `tasks/b-0011/10-workloads.yaml`, `memory: 256Mi` → `64Mi`, targeting `run/gitops-pilot-20260918-141238/b-0011`, `MERGEABLE`, `+1/-1`. Steady state becomes `4x64Mi + 2x64Mi = 384Mi`, leaving `448Mi` headroom, so the blocked pods schedule. Auto-sync applies it on merge.
- **Watch recovery** on the [checkout Deployment](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/deployment/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-20260918-141238/payments/checkout/overview?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) — expect `4/4` Ready and `ReplicaFailure` to clear.
- **Do not raise the quota instead.** It would need `>=1408Mi` (with `maxSurge`), `payments-quota` is platform-team-owned under `CAP-418`, and actual usage is `1Mi` per pod against a `256Mi` request.

**Worth remembering**

- In namespace `payments` on cluster `gitops-pilot-20260918-141238`, ResourceQuota `payments-quota` caps `requests.memory` at `832Mi` and is platform-team-owned under ticket `CAP-418` — raising a per-pod memory request there is a breaking change unless replicas x request is checked against that cap first, and quota changes need platform-team sign-off rather than a workload-team PR.
- The `platform` profile has no `KUBECONFIG` exported, so a bare `kubectl` targets the agent host cluster; per-cluster work must pass `--kubeconfig` from the cluster's profile directory explicitly.
